# Pantoken security assurance case

## Purpose and status

This document explains why Pantoken's documented security requirements are met within the project's
intended use and stated trust model. It identifies the assets and threats considered, the trust
boundaries in the system, the secure-design principles applied, the controls used against common
implementation weaknesses, and the evidence supporting each claim.

This assurance case covers the source repository, the generated outputs, the published npm packages,
the command-line generator, the documentation and demo tooling, and the release process. It should be
read with the [security policy](SECURITY.md) and the
[architecture overview](docs/architecture/overview.md).

The case is intentionally qualified. Pantoken transforms trusted design-system inputs; it is not a
sanitizer or a security boundary for attacker-controlled CSS, JavaScript, JSON, Markdown, HTML,
configuration, or plugin code. Known limitations and improvement work are recorded in
[Residual risks and limitations](#residual-risks-and-limitations).

## Top-level claim

**C0: Pantoken's published packages and generated outputs satisfy the security requirements documented
in `SECURITY.md` when Pantoken is used within its documented trust boundaries.**

The argument for C0 is:

1. The requirements and scope are explicit and testable.
2. The architecture limits runtime dependencies and separates trusted transformation from downstream
   consumption.
3. Controls address the credible threats and common implementation weaknesses in that architecture.
4. Automated tests, analysis, packaging checks, and release attestations provide evidence that the
   controls continue to operate.
5. Residual risks are disclosed rather than silently treated as solved.

## System description

Pantoken resolves Instructure design tokens and icons into a canonical `Token[]` intermediate
representation (IR), vendors that IR as versioned static data, and emits it into formats and
integrations for web frameworks, build systems, design tools, and native platforms.

The principal data flow is:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    upstream["Pinned upstream token and icon sources"]
    core["@pantoken/core transform"]
    ir["Canonical Token[] intermediate representation"]
    tokens["@pantoken/tokens vendored static data"]
    emitters["npm emitters"]
    cli["CLI generators"]
    consumers["Consumer-controlled applications and files"]

    upstream --> core
    core --> ir
    ir --> tokens
    tokens --> emitters
    tokens --> cli
    emitters --> consumers
    cli --> consumers
```

The release path is:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    source["Reviewed repository source"]
    actions["GitHub Actions build and verification"]
    npm["npm trusted publishing and Sigstore provenance"]
    github["GitHub immutable release and release attestation"]

    source --> actions
    actions --> npm
    actions --> github
```

The authoritative architecture description is
[`docs/architecture/overview.md`](docs/architecture/overview.md).

## Assets to protect

Contributor accessibility tooling runs trusted authored examples in a local browser, using
lockfile-pinned automatica11y and locally built styles and scripts. Its reports are advisory evidence,
not security controls or a WCAG certification. Fixtures must not contain credentials or private data.

The security-relevant assets are:

- The integrity of the source repository and release workflow.
- The integrity and provenance of published npm packages and GitHub releases.
- The correctness and reproducibility of the canonical token IR and generated outputs.
- The integrity of consumer files written by the CLI.
- The confidentiality of repository and release credentials.
- The availability of build, documentation, and transformation tools when processing expected inputs.
- The integrity of a consumer process that loads a Pantoken package or plugin.

Pantoken does not hold end-user accounts, passwords, private cryptographic keys, authorization data,
or confidential application data.

# Authoring `@pantoken/components`

`@pantoken/components` is the semantic RSCSS CSS API — a parameterized generator, not hand-written
CSS. Each documented record is one file; the bucket `index.ts` is a barrel + registry, not a monolith.

## Upstream contracts and Figma

Version-matched InstUI source defines upstream component contracts; Instructure design tokens feed
pantoken's canonical IR. Use the existing IR token names and aliases in component CSS. The InstUI
Figma library provides visual evidence and is expected to share that upstream token library, but
versions, bindings, and modes can drift. Report discrepancies and ask before changing public
contracts; don't hide differences with invented tokens or hardcoded values. For library navigation,
MCP retrieval, output ownership, and visual validation, follow the
[Figma workflow in AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md#figma-mcp-integration).

Component ownership follows exports in the workspace's released version of `@instructure/ui`, not
Figma's `Completed` or `Ready for dev` labels. Released components belong in `formats/components`;
`Ready for dev` components absent from those exports belong in `plugins/pantoken/custom-components`.
When adopted upstream, promote them with a functional deprecated custom-components alias for the
existing compatibility period, following the
[promotion policy](build-and-docs.md#upstream-component-follow-up).

## Automatic user preferences

User preferences are intrinsic behavior, not modifiers. Gate decorative transitions and animations
with `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` in each record so standalone sheets and shadow styles
follow the same policy. Keep loading and progress indicators visible when animation stops, and
apply state changes immediately. Interaction behaviors must also respect the live preference:
don't smooth-scroll, delay removal for a skipped fade, or hide progress behind a mount animation.
Do not shorten loading timeouts or cancel announcements in the name of reducing motion.

Token sheets handle color preferences in the active theme's scope. `prefers-contrast: more`
strengthens nonzero border widths and focus rings; `less` removes decorative elevation color without
reducing text contrast. Keep semantic text/status colors and explicit light/dark pins intact.
Links gain an underline in more-contrast mode, including normally unstyled links.

Reduced transparency composites translucent surface tokens over an opaque semantic background.
Remove backdrop blur in that mode, and use opaque muted colors rather than whole-control opacity for
disabled states. Keep intentionally empty backgrounds, image effects, and visibility transitions:
they aren't interchangeable with translucent component chrome. New surface expressions need coverage
in the token preference generator and a real-browser check.

In forced colors, keep browser adjustment on surrounding components and text. Masked glyphs can use
`forced-color-adjust: preserve-parent-color` on the painter itself, with system-color fills. Give
gradient text a solid system-color fallback, and keep selected states visible without shadows.
Native progress needs authored value parts and a CSS-owned indeterminate segment: suppressing CSS
animations alone doesn't stop the browser's built-in loading animation. Check actual rendered pixels,
native range semantics, and live preference changes, including RTL.

- `src/components/<name>/index.ts` + `<name>.css` (`COMPONENTS` registry).
- `src/components/<name>/members/<member>/index.ts` + `<member>.css` — a promoted sub-component (see
  "Sub-components (`@memberOf`)" below).
- `src/utilities/<name>/index.ts` + `<name>.css` (`UTILITIES`).
- `src/rules/{base,prose}/index.ts` + `<name>.css` (`RULES`).
- `src/declarations/<name>/index.ts` + `<name>.css` (`DECLARATIONS`).
- `src/lib/`: `helpers.ts` (ns/scope/glyph consts/spacing scales/`ComponentOptions`/`DEFAULT_PREFIX`),

# TinyMCE Color and Highlight Plugins Plan

## Problem Statement

Currently, pantoken's TinyMCE renderer delegates the `forecolor` (text color) and `hilitecolor` (highlight/background color) commands to TinyMCE's native implementations, which use an unrestricted hex color picker. This creates two issues:

1. **Unlimited palette**: Users can select any hex color, not just pantoken's carefully curated color schemes, breaking design consistency.
2. **Accessibility gap**: The native color picker doesn't enforce WCAG contrast requirements between light/dark theme variants, risking compliance violations.

## Solution Approach

Create two new TinyMCE plugins that replace the native `ForeColor` and `HiliteColor` behaviors with pantoken-aware implementations that:

1. **Constrain the palette** to semantic and primitive color tokens from pantoken's color schemes (rebrand, canvas, canvasHighContrast).
2. **Ensure accessibility** by using contrast-aware color mappings that guarantee WCAG AA compliance for both light and dark modes.
3. **Apply semantic classes** instead of inline styles, following pantoken's existing class-based design patterns.
4. **Maintain parity** with InstUI's design intentions while preserving contrast guarantees.

## Key Design Decisions

### Where colors come from
- Extract available colors from `@pantoken/tokens` (semantic colors) and optionally `@pantoken/plugin-primitives` (raw palette).
- Use the contrast validation utilities already in `packages/utils/color.test.ts` and `packages/core/tests/color.test.ts`.
- The `canvasHighContrast` theme is already designed for accessibility; reuse those color mappings.

### Class-based approach (not inline styles)
- Define classes like `.pantoken-text-color-primary`, `.pantoken-bg-color-primary` instead of applying `color: #hex` styles.
- Align with pantoken's existing philosophy: `@pantoken/components` uses semantic RSCSS CSS with modifiers.
- Classes enable single-point updates (e.g., all "primary" text respects theme changes without re-editing content).

### Light/dark contrast guarantees
- For each light-mode color, compute or retrieve its dark-mode equivalent from the token IR.
- Use the `light-dark()` CSS function available in pantoken tokens to ensure paired light/dark values meet contrast thresholds.
- Validate pairings at build time (new test) to prevent mismatched contrast in live content.

### UI/UX in TinyMCE toolbar
- Offer a color picker that shows only the semantic palette (e.g., "primary", "success", "warning", "error", "neutral").
- Include a visual swatch for each color showing both light and dark preview.
- Optionally also offer the primitive palette as a secondary tier (e.g., in a "more colors" button).
- The picker should be part of a custom TinyMCE UI element (button + dropdown menu).

### 3. **Shared utilities: `plugins/tinymce/color-utils.ts`**

- Exports contrast validation helpers
- Exports class-name generators
- Reusable by both plugins

### 4. **CSS: `renderers/tinymce/src/colors.css` (or integrated into existing sheets)**

- Uses pantoken's token IR and `light-dark()` values

- Unit tests for color palette builder
- Contrast validation tests (new test matrix)
- Integration tests for plugin initialization and command execution
- Snapshot tests for generated classes

- Add API docs for `createForecolorPlugin()` and `createHilitecolorPlugin()`
- Document color class naming convention
- Add example of initializing both plugins in a host app

## TinyMCE Text Color & Highlight — Cleaner Architecture via Reusable Color Plugin

**Refined approach:** Build a reusable `@pantoken/colors` plugin (in `plugins/pantoken/`) that generates accessible color utilities, then have TinyMCE consume it for forecolor/hilitecolor implementations.

### Architecture

**`@pantoken/colors` (build-time Vite plugin):**
- Extracts semantic colors from `@pantoken/tokens` with light/dark pairs
- Validates WCAG AA contrast at build time (4.5:1 text, 3:1 large); fails build if violated
- Emits `.pfx-text-color-<name>` and `.pfx-bg-color-<name>` CSS classes using `light-dark()` function
- Exports runtime color manifest (JSON) with metadata
- Zero TinyMCE dependencies; reusable by other renderers

**TinyMCE Forecolor & Hilitecolor plugins (in `renderers/tinymce`):**
- Consume palette from `@pantoken/colors`
- Replace native `ForeColor`/`HiliteColor` with class-based alternatives
- Register custom picker UI showing semantic colors with light/dark swatches
- Apply `.pfx-text-color-*` or `.pfx-bg-color-*` classes to selections

### Why This Works

1. **Separation of concerns:** Color logic lives once in the plugin; TinyMCE just consumes it
2. **Reusable:** Other renderers can use the same color plugin without TinyMCE coupling
3. **Build-time validation:** Contrast checked once during build, not runtime
4. **Theme-aware:** `light-dark()` CSS ensures automatic switching between light/dark modes
5. **Semantic names:** `sea`, `plum`, `violet`, `custom`—no arbitrary hex codes
6. **Class-based:** Aligns with pantoken's RSCSS philosophy, enables single-point updates

1. **`@pantoken/colors`** — Plugin package with palette extraction, contrast validation, CSS/manifest generation
2. **TinyMCE forecolor & hilitecolor** — Plugins that import the color palette and provide toolbar UI
3. **Tests** — Contrast matrix validation, plugin integration, browser verification
4. **Docs** — Plugin architecture, usage examples, CHANGELOG

1. **Color names:** Confirm set (sea, plum, violet, custom) and whether they vary by theme?
2. **Color source:** Which semantic tokens to include (text-only? background-only? both)?
3. **Class naming:** Fully namespaced (`.instui-text-color-sea`) or modifier-style?
4. **UI swatch style:** Side-by-side light/dark preview or single color?
5. **Backward compat:** Replace default commands entirely, or coexist?
6. **Unknown colors:** Strip, preserve, or map to nearest when pasted into editor?

/** A CSS color: a literal (`#1d354f`, `rebeccapurple`), a `var(--token)`, or a nested helper result. */
export type CssColor = string;

/**
 * Set a color's opacity to `percent`% — the CSS-only mirror of ui-color-utils `alpha`. Mixing with
 * `transparent` yields exactly the color at that alpha channel.
 *
 * @param color - The base color (literal, `var(--token)`, or a nested helper result).
 * @param percent - The target opacity, 0–100.
 * @returns A `color-mix()` expression.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * alpha("var(--brand)", 10); // "color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand) 10%, transparent)"
 * ```
 */
export function alpha(color: CssColor, percent: number): string {
  return `color-mix(in srgb, ${color} ${percent}%, transparent)`;
}

/**

 * (tinycolor lowers HSL lightness). Uses relative color syntax so hue and saturation are preserved.
 *
 * In relative `hsl()`, the `l` channel resolves to a `<number>` on the 0–100 scale — the same scale
 * tinycolor's `amount` uses — so the points are subtracted directly (no `%`).
 *
 * @param color - The base color.
 * @param percent - Lightness points to subtract (default `10`, matching tinycolor's default).
 * @returns An `hsl(from …)` relative-color expression.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * darken("var(--brand)", 10); // "hsl(from var(--brand) h s calc(l - 10))"
 * ```
 */
export function darken(color: CssColor, percent = 10): string {
  return `hsl(from ${color} h s calc(l - ${percent}))`;
}

/**
 * Lighten by `percent` HSL-lightness points — the CSS-only mirror of ui-color-utils `lighten`
 * (tinycolor raises HSL lightness). Uses relative color syntax so hue and saturation are preserved.
 *
 * @param color - The base color.
 * @param percent - Lightness points to add (default `10`, matching tinycolor's default).
 * @returns An `hsl(from …)` relative-color expression.

 * @example

 * lighten("var(--brand)", 10); // "hsl(from var(--brand) h s calc(l + 10))"
 * ```
 */

  return `hsl(from ${color} h s calc(l + ${percent}))`;
}

 * // "color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand) 12%, var(--surface))"
 * ```
 */

  return `color-mix(in srgb, ${overlay} ${percent}%, ${base})`;
}

/**

 * primary-inverse button's text, an icon on a coloured surface): rather than a fixed inverse token,

 *
 * It reads the surface's OKLCH lightness through relative color syntax and snaps it to `0` (black) or

 *
 * @param surface - The background colour content sits on (literal, `var(--token)`, or a nested helper).
 * @param threshold - OKLCH lightness (0–1) above which the surface counts as "light" (default `0.62`).
 * @returns An `oklch(from …)` expression resolving to black or white.

 * // → "oklch(from var(--…-brand) clamp(0, (0.62 - l) * infinity, 1) 0 0)"
 * ```

  return `oklch(from ${surface} clamp(0, (${threshold} - l) * infinity, 1) 0 0)`;

# @pantoken/plugin-colors

CSS-only color math that mirrors the InstUI `@instructure/ui-color-utils` helpers, so derived shades
track pantoken's `var(--instui-*)` tokens at runtime instead of being baked to a fixed hex.

InstUI computes `alpha`, `darken`, `lighten`, and `overlayColors` at build time with `tinycolor2`
against concrete colors. pantoken emits token references that resolve in the browser — often through
`light-dark()` — so the same math has to run in CSS. Each helper returns a CSS color string built on
`color-mix()` and relative color syntax (both Baseline modern-browser features).

## Install

```sh
npm i @pantoken/plugin-colors
```

Also available as `pantoken/colors`.

## Usage

```ts
import { alpha, darken, lighten, overlayColors } from "@pantoken/plugin-colors";

alpha("var(--brand)", 10); // color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand) 10%, transparent)
darken("var(--brand)", 10); // hsl(from var(--brand) h s calc(l - 10))
lighten("var(--brand)", 10); // hsl(from var(--brand) h s calc(l + 10))
overlayColors("var(--surface)", "var(--brand)", 12); // color-mix(in srgb, var(--brand) 12%, var(--surface))
onColor("var(--brand)"); // black or white, whichever reads on the surface (InstUI's *-on-color idea)

// Compose them the way InstUI does — e.g. a brand-tinted ghost-button hover:
const ghostHover = alpha(
  darken("var(--instui-color-institutional-brand-button-primary-bgd)", 10),
  10,
);
```

## Mapping to ui-color-utils

| ui-color-utils (tinycolor)  | This helper     | CSS mechanism                       |
| --------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `alpha(color, percent)`     | `alpha`         | `color-mix()` with `transparent`    |
| `darken(color, percent)`    | `darken`        | `hsl(from …)` relative color syntax |
| `lighten(color, percent)`   | `lighten`       | `hsl(from …)` relative color syntax |
| `overlayColors(c1, c2)`     | `overlayColors` | `color-mix()` (opaque base only)    |
| `*-on-color` token variants | `onColor`       | `oklch(from …)` contrast clamp      |

`darken`, `lighten`, and `overlayColors` cover the RGBA-over-opaque case; general RGBA-over-RGBA
compositing can't be a single CSS color, so it's out of scope. `onColor` mirrors InstUI's recurring
